When refining an item in a refinement list for example, this will trigger 2 network requests because of this implementation.

1. Send request to refine the filter ([see `connectRefinementList` implementation](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/57eaa6056fe0bb7c5e87a8697e7431adbf4042d1/src/connectors/refinement-list/connectRefinementList.js#L308))
2. Send request with the new `ruleContexts` (this line)

I'm not aware of any current way of batching this kind of requests in InstantSearch.

We can provide the default value into the `Renderer` generic.

`FacetRefinement` could be a `number[]`? According to [the Helper doc](https://community.algolia.com/algoliasearch-helper-js/reference.html#AlgoliaSearchHelper.FacetRefinement) it's not possible. What you want is `type Refinement = FacetRefinement | NumericRefinement` no?
We only send one rule context? Is it expected?

Actually after talking a bit with Marie & Julien it might be problematic. We can have a blink:

1. select the refinement -> a request is triggered
2. render with the results, context is applied -> a new request is triggered
3. a query rule is triggered based on the context that set a new filter
4. render with other results, which means that at the step 2 we get stalled results
Is that an acceptable tradeoff for now? (I would say so)
You're right, it makes more sense!
Ok but it doesn't seems that we test the behaviour where we return all the value from a refinement. We only test the behaviour with hard coded value.
It worth trying with a query rule that alter the results to see the actual impact. We can decide then if it's a tradeoff that is acceptable or not.

We test that the function is called with all the values for this: https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/pull/3597/files#diff-1586d17bb858d5402e71bd206ba2d78fR297.

I will add a test that checks that all the values can effectively be tracked.
